deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (my identification). The page works with the fourth-order equation Δ²u = u, with Δ = ∂²/∂x² + ∂²/∂y². This is the Kirchhoff plate-vibration equation Δ²w = k⁴w scaled so that k = 1. The domain is the strip −a < x < a, and the boundary conditions appear to be those of a free edge at x = ±a (Chladni-figure problem).

(1) Splitting. Riemann sets u1 = ½(u − Δu) and u2 = ½(u + Δu). Then:
- Δu1 + u1 = ½(u − Δ²u) = 0.
- Δu2 − u2 = ½(Δ²u − u) = 0.
So u = u1 + u2, with u1 a Helmholtz solution and u2 a modified-Helmholtz solution. That is exactly what the two lines at the top state.

(2) Strip modes, symmetric in x. Take u1 = A cos(√(1−β) x) cos(√β y) and u2 = B cos(√(−1−β) x) cos(√β y). These solve their respective equations since α1² + β = 1 and α2² + β = −1, where α1 = √(1−β) and α2 = √(−1−β).

(3) Boundary conditions. The page (for parameter λ) and the next page (for β, with ν called γ there and B with opposite sign) use:
- (i) νΔu − u_yy = 0 at x = ±a. This gives A(β−ν) cos α1a + B(β+ν) cos α2a = 0.
- (ii) ∂x(νΔu + u_yy) = 0 at x = ±a. This gives A(β+ν) α1 sin α1a + B(β−ν) α2 sin α2a = 0.
On this page the λ-mode is written with −B: A(λ−ν) cos√(1−λ)a − B(λ+ν) cos√(−1−λ)a = 0, and A√(1−λ) sin√(1−λ)a (λ+ν) − B√(−1−λ) sin√(−1−λ)a (λ−ν) = 0.

With ν = 1/(1−σ), where σ is Poisson's ratio (my identification):
- (i) is (1−σ)⁻¹ times (u_xx + σu_yy) = 0.
- (ii) is proportional to u_xxx + (2−σ)u_xyy = 0.
These are Kirchhoff's free-edge conditions. From (i), a β-mode has A_β = (β+ν) cos α2(β)a and B_β = ∓(β−ν) cos α1(β)a. The eigenvalue condition is (β+ν)² α1 sin α1a cos α2a = (β−ν)² α2 sin α2a cos α1a.

(4) Cross pairing. The goal (heading: ∫(u_yy + (λ−?)u) cos√(1−λ)x dx) is a transform that reduces the PDE to ODEs in y, or an orthogonality relation for expanding data in these modes. The next page indeed tries A cos√(1−β)x + B cos√(−1−β)x = f(x).

Riemann pairs the λ-mode coefficients with the β-mode components:
S = A_λ ∫_{−a}^{a} u1^β cos√(1−λ)x dx + B_λ ∫_{−a}^{a} u2^β cos√(−1−λ)x dx.
He uses ∫_{−a}^{a} cos px cos qx dx = 2[p sin pa cos qa − q cos pa sin qa]/(p² − q²). In both integrals p² − q² = β − λ. This gives four terms, each carrying the factor 2c:
- A√(1−λ) sin√(1−λ)a · cos√(1−β)a cos√(−1−β)a (β+ν)/(β−λ)
- B√(−1−λ) sin√(−1−λ)a · (−(β−ν)/(β−λ)) · cos√(1−β)a cos√(−1−β)a
- −A cos√(1−λ)a sin√(1−β)a cos√(−1−β)a √(1−β)(β+ν)/(β−λ)
- −B cos√(−1−λ)a sin√(1−β)a cos√(−1−β)a √(1−β)(β+ν)²/((β−λ)(β−ν))
In the fourth term the β eigenvalue relation was used to trade the √(−1−β) sin√(−1−β)a term for a √(1−β) sin√(1−β)a term.

He then inserts the λ boundary conditions: B√(−1−λ) sin√(−1−λ)a = A√(1−λ) sin√(1−λ)a (λ+ν)/(λ−ν), and A = (λ+ν) cos√(−1−λ)a, B = (λ−ν) cos√(1−λ)a.

First two terms (my algebra): A α1λ sin(α1λ a) C1β C2β [(β+ν)(λ−ν) − (β−ν)(λ+ν)] / ((λ−ν)(β−λ)) = −2ν(λ+ν)/(λ−ν) · α1λ sin α1λa · cos α2λa · C1β C2β. Riemann writes this as the bracket [λ+ν − (λ+ν)²/(λ−ν)] = −2ν(λ+ν)/(λ−ν), noted again at lower left.

Last two terms: −C1λ C2λ α1β sin(α1β a) C2β (β+ν)[(λ+ν)(β−ν) − (λ−ν)(β+ν)] / ((β−λ)(β−ν)) = −2ν C1λ C2λ · (β+ν)/(β−ν) · √(1−β) sin√(1−β)a cos√(−1−β)a.

In both pairs the singular factor β−λ cancels. The result is, up to the factor 2c and sign:
S ∝ −2ν C1λ C2λ C1β C2β [F(λ) + F(β)], with F(t) = (t+ν)/(t−ν) · √(1−t) tan(√(1−t) a).
This is symmetric in λ, β but not zero. So the naive pairing does not make distinct strip modes orthogonal; it leaves a rank-two, sum-separable remainder.

The last line, −A cos√(1−λ)a (β−ν)/(β−λ) + B cos√(−1−λ)a (β+ν)/(β−λ), starts the analogous pairing with the roles of the two boundary conditions exchanged (the boundary-value contributions).
errors: The sign convention for B on this page (−B in both λ conditions) is opposite to the next page (+B). It is internally consistent, so the results are unaffected.
In the first displayed integral the sine argument is written √(x−λ)a; this is a slip for √(1−λ)a.
In the fourth line (−B term), the β eigenvalue relation requires the factor (β+ν)²/(β−ν), not (β+ν)/(β−ν). The image appears to have the square; the transcription drops it.
The marginal factor written (λ+ν)/(β−ν) next to the second combined term should be (β+ν)/(β−ν) by my computation. It is either a slip or a misreading of a β.
In the combined first term the bracket is written with λ instead of β, i.e. [λ+ν − (λ+ν)²/(λ−ν)]. It nevertheless equals the correct value −2ν(λ+ν)/(λ−ν), so the result is right.
The heading integrand (λ−?)u is illegible. The intended transform is never completed on this page.

results.what: Factorisation of Δ²u = u into u1 = ½(u − Δu) solving Δu1 + u1 = 0 and u2 = ½(u + Δu) solving Δu2 − u2 = 0
results.modern_name: Splitting of the plate (biharmonic-Helmholtz) operator Δ² − k⁴ = (Δ + k²)(Δ − k²)

results.what: Symmetric strip modes (A cos√(1−β)x + B cos√(−1−β)x) cos√β y with free-edge conditions νΔu − u_yy = 0 and ∂x(νΔu + u_yy) = 0, i.e. Kirchhoff free-edge conditions with ν = 1/(1−σ), and the resulting frequency equation
results.modern_name: Lévy/Voigt-type separable solutions of the Kirchhoff plate equation with free edges; free-plate (Chladni) strip modes
results.usually_credited_to: Kirchhoff 1850 (boundary conditions); Voigt 1893 and Lévy 1899 (separable rectangular-plate solutions)

results.what: Cross inner product of two distinct free-strip modes, with cancellation of the 1/(β−λ) singularity, giving a nonzero symmetric remainder −2νC1λC2λC1βC2β[F(λ)+F(β)]
results.modern_name: Non-orthogonality/biorthogonality analysis of non-self-adjoint strip eigenfunctions (cf. Papkovich–Fadle expansions)
results.usually_credited_to: Papkovich 1940, Fadle 1941, Smith 1952 (biorthogonality of strip eigenfunctions)

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Riemann working on free-edge Kirchhoff plate vibrations in a strip, decades before Voigt and Lévy, and computing cross-pairings of non-orthogonal strip eigenfunctions in the spirit of later Papkovich–Fadle expansions. However, it is a fragmentary, inconclusive computation: no expansion theorem or biorthogonality relation is reached. Riemann's interest in Kirchhoff-era plate problems is plausible, so this counts as a notable unpublished detail rather than a priority claim.
